A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoORE research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original LLaMA-3.1 8B experiments on CSR-MTL, NLU-MTL, and OR-MTL, together with component ablations and routing-weight analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains those empirical results and adds a full fine-tuning comparison and Qwen-2.5 7B experiments on CSR-MTL.

M1.justification: The SVD-derived rank-one experts, hybrid task/sample router, Householder adapter, and computational procedure remain unchanged. V4 newly documents averaging task embeddings for unseen tasks, but the PDFs do not establish that this changes the procedure used for the existing OR-MTL results.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine CSR-MTL tasks, seven NLU-MTL tasks, and seven OR-MTL tasks, including evaluation on tasks outside the adaptation set. Adding Qwen changes the model configuration, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V4 adds Full Fine-tuning as an evaluated comparator in the LLaMA CSR-MTL table (Table 5). The original adaptation baselines remain, including in the new Qwen comparison. The added SVD-method and O-LoRA discussions do not report empirical comparisons against those methods.

E3.justification: V4 adds a Qwen-2.5 7B evaluation with L values of 0, 2, 4, and 16, plus a control training 100% of LLaMA parameters. The retained experiments' dataset sizes, metrics, few-shot settings, epochs, learning rate, and batch sizes are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 extends the investigation of sensitivity to the number of Householder reflections to Qwen-2.5 7B, supporting an additional robustness assessment across backbones. The original component ablations, task-number analysis, task-correlation heatmap, and routing-weight analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, performance confidence intervals, or significance tests. The routing-weight means and standard deviations across samples in Figures 4–6 retain the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: V4 adds full fine-tuning results of 84.27% overall on LLaMA CSR-MTL and a Qwen result suite, where MoORE achieves 86.31–86.63% overall versus LoRAMoE's 86.17%. These are additional comparisons under their respective model settings. Retained LLaMA benchmark, OR-MTL, and component-ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The full-rank assumption, Equations 1–8, column-space argument, and computational-complexity analysis remain unchanged. The new table summarizing prior SVD methods provides comparative exposition rather than a new derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: SVD-based model MoE-ization, orthogonal experts and column-space preservation, and resistance to task conflict and oblivion. Additional experiments support these retained claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V4 removes the earlier speculation that insufficient task diversity and overfitting explain retention behavior with one to three tasks. It adds discussion of applicability to unseen task IDs and interprets the Qwen results as evidence of architectural robustness. The principal limitations and task-correlation explanation remain.

D1.justification: V4 specifies using the average of nine learned task embeddings for OR-MTL and identifies GPQA, equal batch sizes, and average inference time per batch for the existing timing comparison. These are newly disclosed details; the main hyperparameter table, hardware statement, and code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Section 3.3 and Tables 3–4 substantially expand positioning against SVD-based fine-tuning, comparing SVF, SVDiff, SVFT, KaSA, and SVFCL architecturally and by application. Section 3.2 also distinguishes MoORE from O-LoRA. This fills a significant gap in v1's treatment of closely related approaches and adds explicit novelty-positioning arguments.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the overall section sequence are retained. V4 makes localized introduction and results-discussion edits, adds subsections on SVD comparisons and inference efficiency, inserts the Qwen appendix subsection, and adds acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V4 adds three tables, expands the CSR-MTL table with a full fine-tuning row, and corrects Figure 2's legend from SVDMoE to MoORE. Typography, spacing, and display placement change, while the existing plots retain their data and the document retains its general layout.

improvement.justification: The Qwen evaluation and full fine-tuning control modestly strengthen empirical validation. The expanded SVD/O-LoRA comparisons and explanations of unseen-task routing and timing improve positioning and reproducibility. These are useful but bounded gains: the principal results and theoretical support remain unchanged, and the new performance comparisons still lack run-to-run uncertainty reporting.
